newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares drop 0.47 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares drop 0.47 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to ease in thin and dull trade on Tuesday as the market remained uncertain due to the possibility of an extended new year holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 439.88 points, or 0.47 percent lower at 93,667.24, bringing two day losses to 1.28 percent since Friday's all-time high of 94,879.14 and after last week's 6.2 percent surge.
Traded volume further shrank to nine trillion lira from Monday's 12.96 trillion.

The Turkish government may extend the new year holiday to five days from December 27 to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday. If it does, the Exchange administration must decide whether to close the Exchange on December 30-31.
"There is speculation, even on the possibility of an extended holiday," said Hakan Aksoy from Alfa securities.

Brokers expect buying on the last two days of the week if the holiday is extended to five days because settlements will then be delayed to after the holiday and players can invest in bond repurchase deals for the holiday.
"Several brokerages are also trying to close their trading loans ahead of the year-end which is another factor prompting sales," said Aksoy.
He said hectic activity seen in three utility shares last week also drained cash from the rest of the stocks and caused volume to fall.

The index brushed a low of 92,555 in the afternoon on selling prompted by negative auction results. The Treasury could sell only 69.275 trillion lira of 13-month bonds although it raised the yield by 1.79 points from the previous auction.

Of the 231 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 126 to 53 and 52 ended steady. The 85-share industrial index lost 0.7 percent to 100,738.67 and the 15-share financial index edged 0.08 percent higher to 87,062.04.
Hectic activity in the three utilities faded.
Largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras which gained 1,250 lira to 25,750 made up 13.7 percent of the total turnover.
Brokers said activity in Tupras was due to reports of government plans to introduce an automatic pricing mechanism soon to stop local refineries from making losses.
